subject: Week 27: babyproof before he crawls; Suzuki instrument call due
bodyText:
This week
Days 187-193 open the second half of year one. Sitting usually still leans on hands, with unsupported sitting emerging for some — the CDC checkpoint is 9 months — while pushing to all fours and early commando crawling appear for a subset. Babble picks up intonation ('mamama', 'dadada', still non-referential), he responds to his name, and early stranger anxiety can begin; it typically peaks at 7-10 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Clinging and brief distress around new faces — normal early stranger anxiety, peaking 7-10 months.
- [monitor] A persistent flat spot despite repositioning — pediatricians typically discuss helmet referral around 7-9 months if there is no improvement.
- [call within 24h] Acute illness onset, or feeding refusal that persists across multiple consecutive feeds.
- [call now] Respiratory distress in RSV season — nasal flaring, rib retractions, more than 60 breaths/min at rest, or bluish lips — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Exercise the Suzuki long option this month: pick the instrument (violin, piano, or cello), order the Book 1 recordings and run them 30+ min/day as ambient listening, and join named-teacher waitlists through the Suzuki Association directory — top SF teachers carry multi-year lists, so listing at 6-9 months targets a 2029-2030 lesson start at age 3-4. Cost of the option today: $20-40 of recordings. Suzuki Association of the Americas: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Babyproof ahead of mobility: outlet covers, stair gates at top and bottom, anchored TV and furniture, latched low cabinets, and blind-cord cleats — every cord inaccessible. AAP: Childproofing Your Home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-home/Pages/Childproofing-Your-Home.aspx
- Make pointing-and-naming part of every read — 'Where's the dog? There's the dog' — labeling with joint attention is the mechanism behind read-aloud vocabulary gains. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Rotate in cause-and-effect toys — pop-up boxes, rolling balls, a shape sorter with no sorting agenda — and keep only four to six of the toy library visible at a time; rotation restores novelty for free.

Upcoming
- Nov 26, 2026: first Thanksgiving. If hosting, give him a seat at the table — family meals still count; if traveling, pack the allergen foods you have already cleared so the 2-3x-weekly rotation holds through the trip.
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18–Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit — influenza #2 if this is his first flu season, an iron rescreen, and possibly an ASQ-3 developmental screen. Book after the holidays.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Responds to other people's emotional expressions
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Crying when a parent is sad, brightening when a parent laughs. Foundation of empathy.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-others-emotions/complete

- Distinguishes emotions by tone of voice
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Reacts differently to a stern vs warm voice with the same words.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/distinguishes-emotion-tone/complete

- Finds a partially hidden object
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Beginning of object permanence — fully hidden objects come later.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/finds-partially-hidden-object/complete

- Struggles to reach objects that are out of reach
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Goal-directed behavior. Often precedes intentional rolling or scooting toward an object.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/struggles-for-out-of-reach/complete

- Begins to respond to the word 'no'
  AAP window: day 180-270
  What to look for: Pauses briefly when the word is said. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-no/complete
